name: Jane Hughes
profile: British drug-discovery scientist with ~25 years in target validation, translational research and early clinical development. She was CSO at Gyroscope Therapeutics (acquired by Novartis, 2021) and co-founder/CSO of Aiolos Bio (acquired by GSK, 2024), and now leads science at Verdiva Bio, which develops once-weekly oral GLP-1 and amylin medicines for obesity.
interesting_fact: Verdiva's lead program VRB-101 (oral once-weekly ecnoglutide) is in Phase 2, and in July 2026 it started a Phase 1 trial of VRB-103, a selective oral amylin analog; it was a 2025 Fierce Biotech 'Fierce 15' company.
deep_cut_fact: She began her career at GSK after a PhD in Developmental Immunology at Keele University, later led MedImmune's CNS Cell Biology group, and returned to GSK as Director of Discovery Medicine and translational lead for the antibody otilimab (GSK3196165).
notes: Long-time partner of CEO Khurem Farooq across Gyroscope, Aiolos and Verdiva. Low public profile; route via company/FTI.

name: Jules Urbach
current_role: Founder, CEO & Chairman, OTOY; founder of the Render Network (decentralized GPU rendering)
profile: Los Angeles technologist who founded OTOY in 2008 with Malcolm Taylor; OTOY makes OctaneRender and LightStage capture technology used by VFX studios. He then created the Render Network, a blockchain marketplace that pools idle GPUs for rendering and AI workloads, whose RENDER token gives the project a ~$2B valuation.
interesting_fact: OTOY's advisers have included Eric Schmidt, Brendan Eich, Sam Palmisano and Ari Emanuel; George Gilder called Urbach 'the most inventive software engineer he has ever met.'
deep_cut_fact: His first game was Hell Cab (Time Warner Interactive, 1993), made when he was just 18 and one of the first CD-ROM games ever created; before OTOY he built the web's first 3D game platform, licensed to Disney, Warner Bros., Microsoft and others.
notes: Strong data-center/GPU-compute angle (distributed GPU network for rendering and AI). Frequent conference speaker; personal X account not verified here.

name: Tigrane Seydoux
current_role: Co-founder & co-CEO, Big Mamma Group; co-founder, sunday (restaurant payment app)
profile: Monaco-born French/Monegasque entrepreneur (b. 1984, HEC Paris 2008) who co-founded Italian restaurant group Big Mamma with Victor Lugger in 2015; it grew to 24 restaurants in five countries and sold a majority to McWin in 2023, with the founders remaining co-CEOs. In 2021 he co-founded sunday, a QR-code pay-at-table app that raised $100M and serves 5,000+ restaurants.
interesting_fact: He and Lugger were named Gault & Millau Entrepreneurs of the Year (2017); Big Mamma imports its products directly from Italy, and in 2020 they also launched home-delivery brand Napoli Gang.
deep_cut_fact: His first job after HEC was at Stephane Courbit's online-gaming startup in London, then three years in LOV Group's finance team; he and Lugger first planned a crepe chain but after a month realised they didn't love crepes, only restaurants.
notes: Co-authored cookbook 'Big Mamma: Cuisine italienne, con molto amore' (2016). Avoid family topics.
